title: Alchemist: A Unified Accelerator Architecture for Cross-Scheme Fully Homomorphic Encryption
problem: Existing FHE accelerator architectures with polynomial-level operator abstractions fail to efficiently handle hybrid cross-scheme FHE due to mismatches between computational demands and hardware resources under varying parameter settings.
motivation: Cross-scheme fully homomorphic encryption enables privacy-preserving applications, requiring efficient hardware acceleration for practical deployment.
method: Alchemist introduces Meta-OP, a low-level operator that can handle many different types of polynomial operations (the mathematical building blocks of FHE encryption) while staying hardware-friendly and avoiding complex routing logic. To make this work efficiently, it adds a slot-based data management system that organizes data to match how the hardware accesses memory. This combination lets a single accelerator handle both arithmetic operations (additions, multiplications) and logic operations across different FHE encryption schemes.
key_novelty: Meta-OP is a low-level operator that unifies different polynomial operations across FHE encryption schemes while being hardware-efficient and avoiding complex routing logic.
contributions: Meta-OP operator abstraction supporting diverse polynomial operations across multiple FHE schemes
Slot-based data management scheme for efficient memory access patterns in FHE acceleration
Unified ASIC accelerator supporting both arithmetic and logic FHE workloads
Significant performance gains: 24,829X vs CPU, 29.4X per area vs SOTA (arithmetic), 7.0X vs SOTA (logic)

metrics.ppa: 29.4X performance per area vs SOTA (arithmetic FHE)

limitations: Specific design tradeoffs and limitations not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Unified FHE accelerator with finer-grained operators
